newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch shares took a firm stride higher on Wednesday as Wall Street and the strong dollar combined with better than expected Polygram results and positive views on Philips and Royal Dutch, dealers said.

The AEX index of 25 leading stocks briefly stepped above the 700 mark for the first time on Tuesday, but the index had no trouble galloping past today. It ended up 6.86 points, or 0.98 percent, to 705.58, having earlier reached a new intra-day high of 706.05.
"Yesterday, we made an attempt to break higher. Today, all the factors were positive," one trader said.
Traders were also more upbeat on the two companies that announced results on Wednesday and the two giants due to do so on Thursday.
"Everyone has a slightly brighter view now than they expected," one trader said.

Polygram issued its results pre-bourse to reveal net income down 2.6 percent year-on-year, but at the very top end of analysts' expectations and with profit from films in the second half. It also said it was optimistic it would return to earnings growth in 1997.
Its shares ended up 5.20 guilders, or 6.2 percent, to 88.50

In the afternoon, paper and packaging group KNP BT published its full year results, showing a slide in profits, but a better than expected performance of its paper division. It also foresaw an improvement in profits in 1997.
"It's a good statement for 1997 and it did even a little better than we expected," one trader commented.
Despite the positive outlook, the company's shares only put on 70 cents to 41.10 guilders.
Traders showed little reluctance, however, in buying Philips and Royal Dutch , ahead of the publishing of their full year results on Thursday.

Royal Dutch added 5.80 guilders to 335.80 as the dollar held at or above the 1.89 guilder mark. Traders said a bottoming out of oil prices and a slightly more upbeat feel on Thursday's results had also helped.
Philips, meanwhile, the day's most actively traded stock, was up 4.50 guilders to 78.10.
Some traders said Tuesday's departure of former chairman Jan Timmer from the supervisory board could be the prelude to a major restructuring announcement on Thursday.
"We know the figures will be bad. We want to know the future and the move could be positive long term," one trader said.
A number of call writers in the option market also sought to cover their positions as bullish sentiment mounted.
"There was a short squeeze on the options exchange with Philips," one trader said.
